text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn yesterday intervened in the dispute with farmers from Kiskoros when he invited their representatives to come to his study this afternoon to survey the latest claims and end the disputes.

- Experts speaking on behalf of Hungary on the second day of the Hague trial on the Gabcikovo-Nagymaros hydropower project contended that the project would have been useless and harmful in its original form, not just the "C version" that Slovakia chose in diverting the Danube.
- President Arpad Goncz met President Algirdas Brazauskas of Lithuania yesterday in Vilnius.

- Visiting Prince Philip of Britain said yesterday the World Wildlife Fund will try to help in implementing the ruling to be passed by the International Court of Justice on the Gabcikovo hydropower plant.

- Parliament yesterday acted to implement the 1947 Paris Peace Treaty calling for compensation for Holocaust victims. Ildiko T. Asztalos state secretary at the Ministry of Industry, introduced an advertising bill in Parliament.
- Premier Horn visited the headquarters of Postabank yesterday, stressing that the bank is over its recent crisis.

- Teachers and professors will not take part in any entrance examinations this year, but will go on strike or stage demonstrations unless the cabinet makes an immediate move to have their overdue February salaries paid, as decided at a forum on Tuesday.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The editor in chief of the weekly Demokrata firmly ruled out that an article carried by the paper on February 12 reporting that Postabank was on the brink of collapse, caused last week's rush on the bank's branches.
- The First Hungarian Concession Motorway Rt. is raising the toll on the M1 highway between Gyor and Hegyeshalom from March 20 due to inflation.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The Free Democrat executive body has decided to appoint Culture and Education Minister Balint Magyar to supervise the party's 1998 election campaign.
- Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti told his Czech counterpart in Prague that Hungary is considering buying about 20 L-159 Czech fighter aircraft.
- Magyar Export-Import Bank will have HUF 300 million to allocate as interest subsidy for loans taken out by small and medium-size companies.
- Hungarian institutional investors may subscribe shares of the farm machinery producer Mezogep between March 12-14.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The crawling-peg forint devaluation has achieved its aim of bridging the gap between the internal and external inflation rates, said National Bank President Gyorgy Suranyi.
- The two owners of the Europa-GAN Insurance Company have raised the company's equity from HUF 1 billion to HUF 1.3 billion.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Tourism revenues totalled HUF 345 billion last year.
- The privatisation firm APV Rt. will invite a closed pre-qualification tender for the purchase of Kereskedelmi es Hitelbank by mid-March.
- CIB bank's audited IAS balance sheet showed pre-tax profits of HUF 11.4 billion last year.
